title: Enterprise Onboarding: Comprehensive Support, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended steps, checklists, and operational guidance for enterprise customer onboarding, integration, escalation handling, and recurring health / QBR reviews. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs who participate in onboarding and ongoing account health maintenance.

Scope
- All enterprise customers onboarding to Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers technical integration, SLAs and escalation procedures, common known issues and workarounds, and the quarterly business review (QBR) cadence and artifacts.

Prerequisites
- Signed contract with assigned CSM and SE.
- Technical contact(s) and network admin contact listed in customer record.
- If Private deployment: customer-provided network ranges, VPN details, and KMS/HSM config.

Roles & Ownership
- CSM: overall onboarding timeline, business success metrics, QBR ownership.
- Solutions Engineer: integration validation, API/webhook mapping, security review.
- Support Engineer: triage and incident escalation ownership post-Go-Live.
- SRE/Infra: capacity planning for Dedicated, assistance with Private day-2 ops.

Onboarding Phases (high level)
1) Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Objectives: align success metrics, agree on timeline, share runbooks.
   - Deliverables: Project plan, contact list, access request form (see template below).
2) Integration (Week 1-3)
   - Tasks: API key provisioning, model selection, routing policies, test dataset ingestion.
   - SE checklist: authentication, CORS, webhooks, throughput/latency tests.
3) Validation (Week 3-4)
   - Run perf tests (see Perf Test commands). Validate output quality against customer prompt set.
   - Confirm monitoring (dashboards, alerts) and SLO targets.
4) Go-Live (Week 4)
   - Cutover steps, fallback policy verification, post-launch support window.

Templates & Commands
- Access request (example):
  - email: customer-admin@example.com
  - required: account-id, IAM role, network CIDR, contact name/phone

- Perf test (curl example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \\n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-instruct","input":"<sample prompt>","max_tokens":256}'

Escalation Matrix & Playbook
- Level 1 (Support Tier): Automated triage and first-response (Target response: 1 business hour). Owner: Support Engineers.
- Level 2 (SE/SRE): For degraded performance, partial outages, or reproducible correctness regressions (Target response: 4 business hours). Owner: Solutions Engineering / SRE.
- Level 3 (Engineering / On-call): For production-impacting incidents (SLO violation, regional outage) requiring code or infra changes (Target response: 1 hour). Owner: Eng on-call.

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Acknowledge: Support engineer confirms receipt in ticketing system (Zendesk/Jira) and notifies CSM.
2. Collect telemetry: request logs, request IDs, timestamped traces (example: trace-id: ab12-cdef-2026).
3. Reproduce: run customer prompt against identical model/version & config.
4. Apply mitigations: switch routing policy to host fallback model, scale Dedicated pool, or enable KV cache bypass.
5. Postmortem: document root cause, impact, mitigation, and follow-up items within 72 hours for Sev>2.

SLA & Response Targets
- Critical (production down): initial response 1 hour, mitigation/restore target 4 hours.
- High (severe performance regressions): initial response 4 hours, workaround within 24 hours.
- Medium/Low: response within 1 business day.

Known Issues & Workarounds (selection)
- Symptom: High tail latency for long-sequence generation on Dedicated T4 pools.
  - Likely cause: insufficient request coalescing / long-running KV cache thrash.
  - Workaround: Temporarily pin customers to a smaller max_context length and enable continuous batching=true in customer runtime config. Example config snippet: {
    "max_context":1024,
    "continuous_batching":true
  }
- Symptom: 502 errors when model warming spikes during a canary rollout.
  - Likely cause: cold-starts under high concurrency.
  - Workaround: Add canary pre-warm step and increase min_replicas to 2 for canary group.
- Symptom: Incorrect embedding drift after quantization profile change.
  - Likely cause: mismatched quantization config between training and serving profile.
  - Workaround: Re-run embedding baseline with the new profile and update downstream cosine similarity thresholds.

Support Process & Ticket Lifecycle
- Channeling: Support via customer portal (preferred), email, and PagerDuty for Critical incidents.
- Triage checklist:
  1. Verify customer identity & account ID.
  2. Reproduce with customer-provided prompt and model/version.
  3. Collect request ID, server logs, and relevant traces.
  4. Determine severity and route to the appropriate escalation level.
- Ticket fields required: account_id, contact, model_id, model_version, request_id, timestamps, evidence (logs/traces).

Observability & Dashboards (what to enable)
- Customer-facing dashboards: per-account token usage, 95/99 latency, error rate, recent deploys.
- Alerts (suggested thresholds):
  - 99th percentile latency > 1.5x baseline for 10m -> P1 alert to SRE.
  - Error rate > 1% sustained over 5m -> P1.
  - Token spike > 3x baseline in 15m -> P2 (possible abuse/cost anomaly).

Health Checks & QBR Materials
- Quarterly Health Check (CSM checklist):
  - Adoption metrics: monthly active routes, token growth, feature adoption (streaming / function-calls).
  - Quality metrics: eval regression rate, user-reported accuracy incidents.
  - Cost metrics: per-token unit cost, model mix distribution, quantization savings.
  - Reliability: SLA compliance, incident summary, open action items.
- QBR Agenda (60 minutes):
  1. Executive summary & adoption highlights (10m)
  2. Reliability & incidents since last QBR (10m)
  3. Performance & cost trends (15m)
  4. Roadmap & upcoming feature releases affecting customer (10m)
  5. Action items & next steps (15m)

QBR Templates / Artifacts
- Slide template sections: KPIs, incidents & remediation, optimization opportunities, recommended next steps (cc: SE, Infra, Product).
- Optional deliverables: tailored prompt-eval results, model recommendation memo, dedicated capacity forecast.

Post-Launch Operational Handover
- At 30 days post-Go-Live, SE signs off integration complete and hands off routine ownership to Support + CSM.
- Deliverables: runbook URL, escalation contacts, configured dashboards, and performance baselines.

Appendices
A) Example runbook excerpt (triage reproducibility):
- Step 1: Re-run failing request with identical headers and model_version.
- Step 2: If latency > baseline, snapshot runtime metrics: GPU_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution.
- Step 3: If error=OOM, reduce max_tokens and check quantization profile.

B) Contact matrix (example):
- Support queue: support+enterprise@redwood.ai
- Escalation on-call: pagerduty (link in internal roster)
- SE lead: priya.nair@redwood.ai

Related Documents
- See also: "enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026" for deep-dive integration patterns and API field mappings, and "enterprise-onboarding-escalation-playbook-2025" for historical escalation postmortems.
